headline: Profit surges on volume growth despite Brazil softness
summary_short: Crown Holdings' Q2 2026 revenue was $3,668M (+16.5% y/y, +12.5% q/q) and net income attributable to Crown rose to $245M (+35.4% y/y), with diluted EPS of $2.23 up 42.9% y/y on higher volumes and a lower effective tax rate.
summary_long: Net sales rose on 5% higher beverage-can volumes, pass-through of higher aluminum/material costs ($395M), and favorable FX ($32M). Segment income was mixed: Americas Beverage fell 1% as 14% lower Brazil volumes outweighed 5% higher North America volumes; Europe, Asia Pacific, and Other rose on volumes and operational improvements; Transit Packaging declined on lower volume and inflation. The effective tax rate fell to 24.4% from 26.6% on earnings mix, helping drive net income sharply higher. The company repurchased $283M of stock (leaving ~$800M under its $2B program) and paid a $0.35/share dividend; H1 capex was $203M against a full-year plan of ~$550M. Net leverage was 2.42x, within the 4.5x covenant.

drivers.explanation: Net sales increased primarily due to the pass-through of higher material costs, 5% higher beverage can volumes in both the three- and six-month periods, and favorable foreign currency translation.
